transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Ramesh (Cobalt HoML), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Daniela Ruiz (Security), Alex Tan (Data Scientist)

Brief summary: exploratory discovery about LLM selection (open models vs hosted), context length needs (up to 50k?), multilingual support, and tool-calling / function call patterns. Customer leaning toward private/Dedicated for PII workloads, curious about staged approach (hosted pilot -> Dedicated -> Private/VPC).

Topics: model selection, context window, tool-calling, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (KMS, SOC2, audit logs), rollout strategy, benchmarks.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate y'all making time. quick intro from our side, I'm Sofia, AE on the accounts team, Marcus is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Marcus: hi all, yeah hey, Marcus Lee, SE. we'll try to keep this pretty pragmatic, want to understand your constraints and show where Redwood fits.
[00:20] Priya: thanks. I'll kick off briefly—Cobalt builds analytics for regulated finance clients. Our main point is, we need real-time-ish question answering over customer docs and trade narratives, and we have strict PII rules. we're exploring open models to reduce cost but need enterprise controls.
[00:36] Liam: and platform side we care about latency under 400ms for short queries and predictable throughput for batch jobs. also multilang support — we have EMEA and LATAM customers, so Spanish and Portuguese matter.
[00:49] Daniela: security questions: SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, audit logs and data residency. Also whether logs are kept in any hosted mode.
[00:58] Sofia: perfect, that's the right set. quick clarifying Q: what's your expected token/session length distribution? priya?
[01:05] Priya: most queries are short—like 50-200 tokens—but we also do long syntheses pulling context across many docs, those can be 6k-20k tokens. As we roadmap, we may want up to ~50k for some combined threads. not immediate but on the horizon.
[01:22] Marcus: okay that shapes model choice; many open models have variable context windows. we can support models with 32k contexts and some experimental 64k in Dedicated or Private deployments, depending on quantization.
[01:36] Alex: question — how does KV cache interact with long context? we care about prefix caching to avoid re-tokenizing the same doc chunks.
[01:45] Marcus: our runtime has prefix/KV cache; when you reuse doc prefixes across sessions we can cache keys and reduce token compute. it helps a lot for document search-style flows. caveat: cache footprint and memory depends on sequence length and batch.
[01:58] Liam: about deployment mode — we're thinking pilot on Hosted, then to Dedicated for predictable throughput, and maybe Private for on-prem with sensitive clients. is that a typical path?
[02:10] Sofia: absolutely. many customers do Hosted to validate models quickly, then move to Dedicated reserved capacity once throughput / latency and SLAs matter, and then Private/VPC for regulated customers. we can help with staged rollouts and canary traffic.
[02:23] Daniela: in Hosted, what data is retained? we need assurance that PII isn't stored or that we can opt-out. also SSO with our identity provider.
[02:32] Marcus: Hosted can be configured with no-persist for logs, or with short retention. for enterprise accounts we support VPC/private control plane and KMS integration. SAML/SSO + RBAC are supported. we'll send the security pack after.
[02:44] Priya: model quality—we've benchmarked open models and OpenAI baseline. cost with OpenAI is high, so open models appealing. but tool-calling (like calling our internal scoring API) is a hard requirement. how mature is function calling across open weights?
[03:00] Marcus: function-calling patterns vary. some open weights support structured output much better when you run them with our runtime's function schema enforcement. we provide tool-calling helpers — you can define a schema and the runtime will map tokens to structured calls. gaps exist for some distilled weights where output formatting is noisy.
[03:15] Alex: do you have examples of tool-calling with open models? especially multilingual function responses.
[03:21] Marcus: yes, we can share a few demo runs. usually for robust function calls we recommend slightly larger models or quantization profiles that preserve output distribution. also, you can combine classification models for intent detection plus a generation model for the actual text.
[03:35] Liam: latency — you mentioned 400ms target for short queries. can Redwood hit that with dedicated pools?
[03:42] Marcus: with Dedicated and optimized batching we can hit sub-200ms for short prompts on smaller models (Llama 2 13B-type) depending on sequence length and kernel selection. for larger models or longer contexts, latency will rise. there's always tradeoff: smaller model + careful prompt engineering = lower latency, but possibly lower quality.
[03:59] Priya: our quality bar is high for financial summaries — hallucination is a big risk. do you support eval suites and regressions?
[04:07] Sofia: yes, Redwood Optimize offers eval tooling to track quality regressions tied to prompt sets. we can run continuous evals and set alerts for quality drops after model swaps or quantization changes.
[04:18] Daniela: talking about quantization—how safe is 4-bit quant for us? we need deterministic behavior for audits.
[04:25] Marcus: quantization can slightly change outputs; for most workloads 4-bit is fine, but for sensitive summarization you may prefer 8-bit or fp16 in Dedicated/Private. we can recommend quant profiles per workload and run A/B to measure drift.
[04:40] Alex: any constraints on batch sizes and concurrency? we have peaks during batch job windows.
[04:47] Marcus: Dedicated pools support autoscaling, and we expose concurrency controls and burst capacity. autoscale policies can be schedule-based or based on queue metrics. for predictable peaks you can reserve capacity.
[04:59] Liam: about model variants — can we run different models by route? e.g., low-latency model for short queries and heavy model for long syntheses?
[05:07] Marcus: yes, routing policies allow per-route model pins, with fallbacks. you can have a cheap low-latency model for the chat route and a larger context model for the synth route; Redwood will fallback to a compatible variant if the preferred model is unavailable.
[05:20] Priya: this is great. what's the typical timeline to go from pilot to Dedicated?
[05:26] Sofia: usually pilot is 2-4 weeks (hosted), then Dedicated provisioning takes a couple weeks depending on capacity, SLA negotiation for enterprise can add time. Private on-prem will extend timeline due to networking and security reviews.
[05:38] Daniela: we need proof points on compliance — do you have SOC2 cert and pen test reports?
[05:44] Sofia: yes, we'll share our SOC2 report, pen test summary, and KMS/HSM integration docs. for Private deployments we can support customer-managed KMS.
[05:55] Liam: curious on cost math — can you send a per-token cost comparison between Hosted and Dedicated, and a model sizing recommendation for our load?
[06:03] Sofia: will do; Marcus will size based on your hit rates / token distribution once you share sample prompts and volume.
[06:10] Alex: we have a question on multilingual quality — Spanish/Portuguese performance tends to drop on some models. any recommendations?
[06:18] Marcus: often larger multilingual models or fine-tuned variants help. we can benchmark the top candidates (Mistral-like, Llama 2 derivatives, some specialized multilingual weights). we also have tokenizers and byte-level handling that affect languages with diacritics. we'll include that in the benchmark.
[06:33] Priya: for the pilot, what would you need from us?
[06:36] Sofia: 1) canonical prompt set (10-20 prompts) across short and long workflows; 2) expected RPS and batch windows; 3) any PII examples (synthetic) to test redaction and KMS; 4) security questionnaire.
[06:48] Priya: ok we'll pull those together.
[06:51] Marcus: also helpful if you can share sample doc sizes so we can recommend context window and storage.
[06:56] Liam: last thing — tool-calling security. when a model calls an internal API, does Redwood proxy that or do you recommend direct calls?
[07:04] Marcus: we support both. many customers run a lightweight middleware that validates function-call payloads; Redwood can also offer a secure proxy pattern with auditing and rate limiting. for Private deployments you can keep everything within VPC.
[07:18] Daniela: can you log function-call arguments? for audits we need traceability but also PII redaction.
[07:25] Marcus: yes, you can log with redaction rules; we also support token-level cost traces and request-level audit logs. retention and redaction are configurable for enterprise accounts.
[07:36] Sofia: ok, quick recap and next steps. We'll: 1) send pilot pricing + Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison, 2) Marcus will assemble a recommended benchmark harness and suggested prompt set, 3) send security pack (SOC2, SSO, KMS docs).
[07:52] Priya: we'll send prompts, synthetic PII, and expected RPS. Let's aim to review the pilot proposal next Thursday.
[08:00] Sofia: sounds good. any final Qs?
[08:03] Alex: just one — do you have sample latency numbers for 13B vs 70B on Dedicated?
[08:09] Marcus: yes, we'll include a small table in the follow-up. short answer: 13B can be sub-200ms on short prompts; 70B is higher and often better for heavy syntheses but with more cost.
[08:22] Daniela: thanks everyone.
[08:24] Sofia: appreciate it, we'll follow up. bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and minor ASR errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Mistral-like" tokenization variations).

End of transcript.
